title: Battle of Lake Trasimene
summary: Spring the ambush and capture both Roman field camps within twenty minutes, before the mist lifts and a cohort escapes the basin.
teaching_goal: A nation stands on its commander. Kill him and the camps go quiet and unclaimed - which, against a twenty-minute clock, is the only version of this battle that finishes in time.
narrative_intent: The Roman column walks into a geographical trap and is destroyed by converging attacks while the lakeside Sepulcher altar remains an optional horror.
historical_context: 217 BC: Hannibal drew Gaius Flaminius along the narrow northern shore of Lake Trasimene and attacked from concealed high ground in morning mist. The Roman marching column had little room to deploy and Flaminius was killed.

victory_conditions.description: Seize both Roman camps. The ambush is not finished until their flags come down.
Kill every enemy commander. A nation dies with the man who leads it: its camps fall neutral, its works come down and its troops leave the field.

defeat_conditions.description: Twenty minutes before the mist lifts. If a cohort clears the basin, Rome learns the shape of the trap.
Your camp falls — the field goes with it.
Every soldier lost is counted by the enemy tonight.
The commander falls — and every line collapses behind him.
A general alone on a dead field is just the last corpse standing.

optional_objectives.description: Crush both Roman breakout columns before they claw through the hillside.

stages.title: Close the trap on the column town
stages.description: Take the Roman marching town at the head of the lakeside road.
stages.hint: The road runs north-west along the shore; strike the head of the column first.

stages.title: Take the shore camp
stages.description: Seize the second camp at the eastern end of the lake.
stages.hint: Nothing on the shore road survives once both ends are held.

stages.title: Kill the Roman commanders
stages.description: Flaminius must not leave the shore.
stages.hint: Their camps fall neutral once their commander is dead.

actions.text: The Roman column enters the corridor. Wait for full commitment.
Strike now. Close the western route and split their line.
Roman cavalry is attempting a breakout from the south. Intercept them.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_legion_organizer
commander_messages.text: Mist on a lake road. Flaminius holds that a column moves faster than an ambush can close, and he is a consul, so he must be right. Do enjoy the next hour. I shall be the one writing the account of it.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_legion_organizer
commander_messages.text: Fifteen thousand in the shallows, and the augurs will say the sacred chickens warned us. Kill a consul and Rome elects another by market day. That is the trick of us: we are not a man.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_legion_organizer
commander_messages.text: The mist lifted a little early for you. It happens. The lake will keep what it has been given, and the thing beneath the altar on the shore is not particular about whose it is.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_legion_organizer
commander_messages.text: You have the marching town. Flaminius built it in a fog and never looked back. There is a lesson there; he will not be the one to learn it.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: The shore camp. That was the way out, and now there is only the lake. Romans are not, on the whole, a swimming people.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_legion_organizer
commander_messages.text: The column is on the lakeside road. In fog, in a defile, in a hurry. Every word of that sentence is a mistake and Flaminius owns them all.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: Somebody is trying to cut a way out along the shore. Good. Somebody should get home and describe this accurately.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_legion_organizer
commander_messages.text: They are hitting your camp, because it is the only thing on this road they can see. Men in fog attack whatever is nearest. Remember it.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_legion_organizer
commander_messages.text: Your men are dying too. A trap costs the trapper something; the good ones simply cost him less.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_legion_organizer
commander_messages.text: So he dies by his own lake in his own fog. Rome will call it justice. I call it weather, and I have always respected weather.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_legion_organizer
commander_messages.text: The column is nearly gone. What is left of it will hold until the fog lifts, because that is the only order anyone can still hear.

theme: Legions march in column through the shoreline corridor — and the hills swallow them whole.
